# Excel (Microsoft 365) MCP connector

Let your AI work with Excel workbooks in OneDrive and SharePoint: list sheets, read any range or a sheet's used range, write values and formulas, read and append table rows, add sheets and create tables. The AnythingMCP connector gives Claude, ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot, Cursor and Gemini 15 MCP tools for Excel (Microsoft 365): 9 read and 6 can change data.

[![Open Excel (Microsoft 365) in AnythingMCP Cloud](https://img.shields.io/badge/Open%20in-AnythingMCP%20Cloud-1f6feb?style=for-the-badge)](https://cloud.anythingmcp.com/login?mode=register&redirect=%2Fconnectors%2Fstore%3Finstall%3Dmicrosoft-excel&utm_source=github&utm_medium=catalog&utm_campaign=microsoft-excel)

## Start without code

No installation and no terminal: AnythingMCP Cloud runs the Excel (Microsoft 365) connector for you, operated by helpcode.ai in Frankfurt, Germany.

1. **Click the button above** and create an account or sign in. The Excel (Microsoft 365) connector opens, ready to install.
2. **Sign in with your Excel (Microsoft 365) account** when AnythingMCP asks. The first time, an admin creates a small app in the Excel (Microsoft 365) developer console. Every click is in the [step-by-step guide](https://anythingmcp.com/guides/microsoft-excel-to-mcp).
3. **Click Install.** AnythingMCP shows the address of your MCP server.
4. **Add that address to your assistant:** [Claude](https://anythingmcp.com/guides/connect-microsoft-excel-to-claude) · [ChatGPT](https://anythingmcp.com/guides/connect-microsoft-excel-to-chatgpt) · [Microsoft Copilot](https://anythingmcp.com/guides/connect-microsoft-excel-to-copilot) · [Cursor](https://anythingmcp.com/guides/connect-microsoft-excel-to-cursor) · [Gemini CLI](https://anythingmcp.com/guides/connect-microsoft-excel-to-gemini) · [Meta Muse](https://anythingmcp.com/guides/connect-microsoft-excel-to-muse).
5. **Ask your first question**, for example: *Do we have invoice INV-2026-045 for Nordic Furnishings Oy in Accounts/AR_2026.xlsx, and what's its status and amount?*

Prefer help with the setup? [Talk to us](https://anythingmcp.com/contact).

## How it works

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  client["Claude · ChatGPT · Copilot · Cursor"]
  amcp["AnythingMCP<br/>roles · audit log · encrypted credentials"]
  api["Excel (Microsoft 365) API<br/>graph.microsoft.com"]
  client -- "MCP, OAuth or API key" --> amcp
  amcp -- "HTTPS, an OAuth 2.0 access token, refreshed automatically" --> api
```

- **The AI client** speaks MCP (Streamable HTTP) to AnythingMCP and only sees tool names, descriptions and results. It never gets the Excel (Microsoft 365) credentials.
- **AnythingMCP** checks the client's role, builds the call from the tool definition, adds the credentials (an OAuth 2.0 access token, refreshed automatically), calls Excel (Microsoft 365), logs the call and returns the result.
- **Excel (Microsoft 365)** sees an ordinary API client with the rights of the account the credentials belong to.

## Tool reference

Every parameter as the AI client sees it in `tools/list`. Source: [`packages/backend/src/adapters/intl/microsoft-excel.json`](../../../packages/backend/src/adapters/intl/microsoft-excel.json).

### `excel_get_my_drive`

Get the signed-in user's OneDrive: its id (the drive_id for workbooks stored there), type and owner. A cheap check that the connector works.

**Access:** read · **Call:** `GET /me/drive`

No parameters.

### `excel_find_workbooks`

Search the user's OneDrive for workbooks by name or content, e.g. "budget" or "xlsx". Returns id, name, parentReference.driveId (the drive_id the other tools need), size, dates and webUrl. Only .xlsx files work with the workbook tools. Paginate with skip_token.

**Access:** read · **Call:** `GET /me/drive/root/search(q='{query}')`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `query` | string | yes | Search text, matched against file names, metadata and content, e.g. "budget 2026". Write a single quote as two (''), e.g. "O''Brien". |
| `top` | integer | no | Items per page (Graph's default is 200 for folders and lists). |
| `skip_token` | string | no | To fetch the next page, pass the $skiptoken (or skipToken) value from the @odata.nextLink of the previous response, with the same other arguments. |

### `excel_get_workbook_by_path`

Look up a workbook in the user's OneDrive by path, e.g. "Documents/Budget 2026.xlsx", and return its id and parentReference.driveId for the other tools.

**Access:** read · **Call:** `GET /me/drive/root:/{path}`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | yes | Path from the top of the OneDrive without a leading slash, e.g. "Finance/Budget 2026.xlsx". Names containing #, % or ? cannot be addressed by path: use excel_find_workbooks. |

### `excel_list_worksheets`

List the worksheets (tabs) of a workbook: id, name, position (0-based) and visibility. Call it first to learn the sheet names.

**Access:** read · **Call:** `GET /drives/{drive_id}/items/{item_id}/workbook/worksheets`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `drive_id` | string | yes | Drive id of the workbook: parentReference.driveId from excel_find_workbooks or excel_get_workbook_by_path, or the id from excel_get_my_drive for the user's own OneDrive. For a SharePoint library, the drive id from the SharePoint connector's sharepoint_list_drives. |
| `item_id` | string | yes | Drive item id of the .xlsx file, from excel_find_workbooks or excel_get_workbook_by_path. |

### `excel_read_range`

Read a range of one worksheet, e.g. "A1:D20": returns address and values (a list of rows, numbers as numbers, dates as serial numbers) by default, plus text, formulas or numberFormat when asked through fields. Output over 200 KB is cut and marked _truncated: read big sheets in blocks of rows.

**Access:** read · **Call:** `GET /drives/{drive_id}/items/{item_id}/workbook/worksheets/{worksheet}/range(address='{address}')`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `drive_id` | string | yes | Drive id of the workbook: parentReference.driveId from excel_find_workbooks or excel_get_workbook_by_path, or the id from excel_get_my_drive for the user's own OneDrive. For a SharePoint library, the drive id from the SharePoint connector's sharepoint_list_drives. |
| `item_id` | string | yes | Drive item id of the .xlsx file, from excel_find_workbooks or excel_get_workbook_by_path. |
| `worksheet` | string | yes | Worksheet name (e.g. "Sheet1", "Sales 2026") or id, from excel_list_worksheets. |
| `address` | string | yes | Cell range in A1 notation without the sheet name, e.g. "A1:D20", "B2", "A:C" (whole columns) or "2:5" (whole rows). |
| `fields` | string | no | Range properties to return, comma-separated: address, values, text (as displayed), formulas, numberFormat, valueTypes, rowCount, columnCount, rowIndex, columnIndex. |

### `excel_read_used_range`

Read the part of a worksheet that holds values (its used range): address (e.g. Sheet1!A1:F120), rowCount, columnCount and values. Use it to learn a sheet's size before reading blocks. Output over 200 KB is cut and marked _truncated.

**Access:** read · **Call:** `GET /drives/{drive_id}/items/{item_id}/workbook/worksheets/{worksheet}/usedRange(valuesOnly=true)`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `drive_id` | string | yes | Drive id of the workbook: parentReference.driveId from excel_find_workbooks or excel_get_workbook_by_path, or the id from excel_get_my_drive for the user's own OneDrive. For a SharePoint library, the drive id from the SharePoint connector's sharepoint_list_drives. |
| `item_id` | string | yes | Drive item id of the .xlsx file, from excel_find_workbooks or excel_get_workbook_by_path. |
| `worksheet` | string | yes | Worksheet name (e.g. "Sheet1", "Sales 2026") or id, from excel_list_worksheets. |
| `fields` | string | no | Range properties to return, comma-separated: address, values, text (as displayed), formulas, numberFormat, valueTypes, rowCount, columnCount, rowIndex, columnIndex. |

### `excel_update_range`

Write into a range, overwriting what is there: values, or formulas (e.g. [["=SUM(B2:B20)"]]), and optionally numberFormat. The arrays must have exactly the range's rows and columns ("A1:B2" takes 2 rows of 2). Returns the range with its new values.

**Access:** write · **Call:** `PATCH /drives/{drive_id}/items/{item_id}/workbook/worksheets/{worksheet}/range(address='{address}')`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `drive_id` | string | yes | Drive id of the workbook: parentReference.driveId from excel_find_workbooks or excel_get_workbook_by_path, or the id from excel_get_my_drive for the user's own OneDrive. For a SharePoint library, the drive id from the SharePoint connector's sharepoint_list_drives. |
| `item_id` | string | yes | Drive item id of the .xlsx file, from excel_find_workbooks or excel_get_workbook_by_path. |
| `worksheet` | string | yes | Worksheet name (e.g. "Sheet1", "Sales 2026") or id, from excel_list_worksheets. |
| `address` | string | yes | Cell range in A1 notation without the sheet name, e.g. "A1:D20", "B2", "A:C" (whole columns) or "2:5" (whole rows). |
| `values` | any[][] | no | Rows of cell values, e.g. [["Date", "Amount"], ["2026-10-09", 120.5]]. Each inner list is one row and every row must have the same number of cells. A value starting with = is entered as a formula. |
| `formulas` | any[][] | no | Rows of formulas in English notation, e.g. [["=A2*1.19"]], instead of values. |
| `number_format` | string[][] | no | Rows of Excel number formats, e.g. [["0.00", "dd/mm/yyyy"]]. |

### `excel_add_worksheet`

Add a worksheet (tab) at the end of the workbook. Returns its id, name, position and visibility.

**Access:** write · **Call:** `POST /drives/{drive_id}/items/{item_id}/workbook/worksheets/add`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `drive_id` | string | yes | Drive id of the workbook: parentReference.driveId from excel_find_workbooks or excel_get_workbook_by_path, or the id from excel_get_my_drive for the user's own OneDrive. For a SharePoint library, the drive id from the SharePoint connector's sharepoint_list_drives. |
| `item_id` | string | yes | Drive item id of the .xlsx file, from excel_find_workbooks or excel_get_workbook_by_path. |
| `name` | string | yes | Name of the new sheet, unique in the workbook, at most 31 characters, without : \ / ? * [ ]. |

### `excel_list_tables`

List the tables (formatted Excel tables) of a workbook: id, name, showHeaders, showTotals and style. Table rows are read and appended with excel_list_table_rows and excel_add_table_rows.

**Access:** read · **Call:** `GET /drives/{drive_id}/items/{item_id}/workbook/tables`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `drive_id` | string | yes | Drive id of the workbook: parentReference.driveId from excel_find_workbooks or excel_get_workbook_by_path, or the id from excel_get_my_drive for the user's own OneDrive. For a SharePoint library, the drive id from the SharePoint connector's sharepoint_list_drives. |
| `item_id` | string | yes | Drive item id of the .xlsx file, from excel_find_workbooks or excel_get_workbook_by_path. |

### `excel_list_table_columns`

List a table's columns: id, name (the header text) and index. Use it to put values in the right order before adding rows.

**Access:** read · **Call:** `GET /drives/{drive_id}/items/{item_id}/workbook/tables/{table}/columns`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `drive_id` | string | yes | Drive id of the workbook: parentReference.driveId from excel_find_workbooks or excel_get_workbook_by_path, or the id from excel_get_my_drive for the user's own OneDrive. For a SharePoint library, the drive id from the SharePoint connector's sharepoint_list_drives. |
| `item_id` | string | yes | Drive item id of the .xlsx file, from excel_find_workbooks or excel_get_workbook_by_path. |
| `table` | string | yes | Table name (e.g. "Table1") or id, from excel_list_tables. |

### `excel_list_table_rows`

Read the data rows of a table (without the header): each row's index and values. Page with top and skip. Output over 200 KB is cut and marked _truncated.

**Access:** read · **Call:** `GET /drives/{drive_id}/items/{item_id}/workbook/tables/{table}/rows`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `drive_id` | string | yes | Drive id of the workbook: parentReference.driveId from excel_find_workbooks or excel_get_workbook_by_path, or the id from excel_get_my_drive for the user's own OneDrive. For a SharePoint library, the drive id from the SharePoint connector's sharepoint_list_drives. |
| `item_id` | string | yes | Drive item id of the .xlsx file, from excel_find_workbooks or excel_get_workbook_by_path. |
| `table` | string | yes | Table name (e.g. "Table1") or id, from excel_list_tables. |
| `top` | integer | no | Rows to return. |
| `skip` | integer | no | Rows to skip from the top of the table, for the next page. |

### `excel_add_table_rows`

Append rows at the end of a table (or insert them at a 0-based index); the table grows and formulas and formats of the table columns carry over. values is a list of rows with one value per table column. Add many rows in one call rather than one at a time. Work or school accounts only.

**Access:** write · **Call:** `POST /drives/{drive_id}/items/{item_id}/workbook/tables/{table}/rows`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `drive_id` | string | yes | Drive id of the workbook: parentReference.driveId from excel_find_workbooks or excel_get_workbook_by_path, or the id from excel_get_my_drive for the user's own OneDrive. For a SharePoint library, the drive id from the SharePoint connector's sharepoint_list_drives. |
| `item_id` | string | yes | Drive item id of the .xlsx file, from excel_find_workbooks or excel_get_workbook_by_path. |
| `table` | string | yes | Table name (e.g. "Table1") or id, from excel_list_tables. |
| `values` | any[][] | yes | Rows of cell values, e.g. [["Date", "Amount"], ["2026-10-09", 120.5]]. Each inner list is one row and every row must have the same number of cells. A value starting with = is entered as a formula. |
| `index` | integer | no | Optional 0-based position among the data rows; rows below move down. Default: the end. |

### `excel_create_table`

Turn a range into an Excel table, e.g. address "Sheet1!A1:D1" with has_headers true to start an empty table from a header row. Returns the table's id and name (Table1, Table2...).

**Access:** write · **Call:** `POST /drives/{drive_id}/items/{item_id}/workbook/tables/add`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `drive_id` | string | yes | Drive id of the workbook: parentReference.driveId from excel_find_workbooks or excel_get_workbook_by_path, or the id from excel_get_my_drive for the user's own OneDrive. For a SharePoint library, the drive id from the SharePoint connector's sharepoint_list_drives. |
| `item_id` | string | yes | Drive item id of the .xlsx file, from excel_find_workbooks or excel_get_workbook_by_path. |
| `address` | string | yes | Range with the sheet name, e.g. "Sheet1!A1:D1" or "'Sales 2026'!A1:F50". |
| `has_headers` | boolean | yes | true when the first row of the range holds the column names. |

### `excel_clear_range`

Clear a range: its contents, its formats, or both. Cannot be undone through the API, only from the file's version history. Installed switched off.

**Access:** write · **Call:** `POST /drives/{drive_id}/items/{item_id}/workbook/worksheets/{worksheet}/range(address='{address}')/clear`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `drive_id` | string | yes | Drive id of the workbook: parentReference.driveId from excel_find_workbooks or excel_get_workbook_by_path, or the id from excel_get_my_drive for the user's own OneDrive. For a SharePoint library, the drive id from the SharePoint connector's sharepoint_list_drives. |
| `item_id` | string | yes | Drive item id of the .xlsx file, from excel_find_workbooks or excel_get_workbook_by_path. |
| `worksheet` | string | yes | Worksheet name (e.g. "Sheet1", "Sales 2026") or id, from excel_list_worksheets. |
| `address` | string | yes | Cell range in A1 notation without the sheet name, e.g. "A1:D20", "B2", "A:C" (whole columns) or "2:5" (whole rows). |
| `apply_to` | `All` \| `Contents` \| `Formats` | no | What to clear: "Contents" (values and formulas), "Formats" or "All" (default). |

### `excel_delete_worksheet`

Delete a worksheet with everything on it. Cannot be undone through the API, only from the file's version history. Installed switched off.

**Access:** write · **Call:** `DELETE /drives/{drive_id}/items/{item_id}/workbook/worksheets/{worksheet}`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `drive_id` | string | yes | Drive id of the workbook: parentReference.driveId from excel_find_workbooks or excel_get_workbook_by_path, or the id from excel_get_my_drive for the user's own OneDrive. For a SharePoint library, the drive id from the SharePoint connector's sharepoint_list_drives. |
| `item_id` | string | yes | Drive item id of the .xlsx file, from excel_find_workbooks or excel_get_workbook_by_path. |
| `worksheet` | string | yes | Worksheet name (e.g. "Sheet1", "Sales 2026") or id, from excel_list_worksheets. |

## Run it yourself

AnythingMCP is open source (AGPL-3.0). [Run it with Docker](../../../README.md#run-it-yourself), open **Connectors → Store**, pick **Excel (Microsoft 365)** and enter `MICROSOFT_CLIENT_ID`, `MICROSOFT_CLIENT_SECRET`, `MICROSOFT_TENANT_ID`, then add your MCP server URL to the AI client.
